structure: Main prediction: the waiter is about to slip on the puddle.
Second prediction: the pot boiling over and the chef not noticing.
Third prediction: the flames and smoke setting off the smoke alarm.
Overall consequence: the dinner rush (tickets, clock) means delays for customers.
modelAnswer: I think things are about to go wrong in this kitchen. First of all, a waiter in a black vest is carrying a really tall stack of plates in one hand, and the stack is already leaning. He's heading toward the door to the dining room, but there's a puddle of water right in front of him, and he doesn't seem to have noticed it. So he'll probably slip, and most of those plates will smash on the floor. Meanwhile, on the stove, a pot is boiling over, and the chef, who's busy with a frying pan, might not notice until there's a mess everywhere. Also, the flames from his pan are shooting up really high, and smoke is rising toward the smoke detector on the ceiling, so I wouldn't be surprised if the alarm goes off. With all those order tickets piling up and the clock showing seven, it's clearly the dinner rush, so these accidents will slow everything down, and customers will end up waiting longer for their food.

usefulExpressions.expression: Things are about to go wrong
usefulExpressions.usageVi: Mọi chuyện sắp trục trặc — câu mở đầu dự đoán tổng quát
Có vẻ chưa để ý thấy — giải thích vì sao tai nạn sẽ xảy ra
Trong khi đó — chuyển sang một khu vực/dự đoán khác
Tôi sẽ không ngạc nhiên nếu… — dự đoán ở mức khá chắc chắn, nghe tự nhiên
Rốt cuộc phải chờ lâu hơn — nói hậu quả cuối cùng

commonMistakes: Dùng 'will' cho mọi câu nghe đơn điệu; hãy xen kẽ 'is going to', 'will probably', 'might', 'I wouldn't be surprised if'.
Sau 'if' không dùng 'will': 'if the alarm will go off' → 'if the alarm goes off'.
Dùng 'plate' số ít cho cả chồng đĩa; nói 'a stack of plates'.
